item.title: auto exits silently when session processes zero items — no actionable guidance shown
item.intent: When an auto session ends with zero items processed, a session-level message must be shown stating how many items were skipped and why, with a suggested remediation command.
item.description: When all items in an auto session are skipped (intent gate, not ready, or dependencies unmet), the session exits with no session-level summary. After BUG-100 adds per-item skip warnings, users will see individual warning lines but no closing message directing them to fix the backlog. A user who runs 'auto done' and sees 0 items processed needs the session to close with: 'Session complete: 0 of N items processed. X items skipped for intent issues — run backlog check --all to audit readiness.' This closes the feedback loop that BUG-100 opens.
steps: In cmd_auto (or the sprint loop exit path), after the loop ends, check if items_processed == 0
If zero items were processed, print: log_warn 'Session ended: 0 items processed. Check backlog readiness with: aishore backlog check --all'
Include the count of items that were available but skipped if that count is available from the loop state
If items_processed > 0 but less than queued, still show the normal summary (BUG-122 end-of-session table) — no change needed for the success path
acceptanceCriteria: Running 'auto done' when all items lack intent shows per-item warnings (BUG-100) plus a session-level closing message with remediation hint
Running 'auto done' when some items succeed shows the normal summary table with no extra warning
Running 'auto done' with an empty backlog shows the existing 'no items' message unchanged
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
